minutes.headline: Committee reorganized, lifted the hiring freeze on budgeted positions, then went into executive session on union talks.
minutes.summary: The School Committee reorganized after the election, choosing a chair, vice chair and secretary, and voted subcommittee assignments as a slate. It removed the hiring freeze, approved year-end encumbrances, the FY21 meeting calendar and an unaffiliated staff salary schedule. The superintendent updated on reopening plans, and the meeting ended in executive session on collective bargaining.

public_comment.topic: Urged the committee, ahead of union negotiations, to restrain teacher salary growth and consider dropping top steps of the contract; said school budget growth is not sustainable.

budget_items.what_was_said: Annual authorization for each school's student activity account, same as last year.
Business manager asked to lift the freeze on positions budgeted in the June budget; new positions would still need committee justification of funding.
Business manager said the budget is very tight and double-budgeting a retiring teacher's overlap is probably unaffordable.
Open purchase orders are unusually high this year because of facilities, PPE, bus and van pool orders and a grant.
No increases for permanent staff; junior aide rates follow minimum wage from January and cafeteria monitor steps are cut to three.
Resident said salary increases are unsustainable for the school budget.

decisions.decision: Hold a special meeting after state transportation and sports guidance is released, on 48-hour notice, and keep regular August meetings.
Superintendent will send a Doodle poll to set a second August workshop date; superintendent evaluation workshop to be separate from the governance workshop.
Superintendent will survey families and staff on reopening after the holiday weekend.

what_happened.line: The School Committee voted to permanently remove the hiring freeze, so positions funded in the June budget can be filled.
The committee approved the year-end encumbrances carried from FY20 into FY21 as presented, with the chair abstaining.
The committee approved a salary schedule for unaffiliated staff with no increases for permanent staff.
The committee approved the FY21 meeting calendar, with regular August meetings kept and a special meeting planned once state guidance is out.
After reorganizing and electing a chair, vice chair and secretary, the committee voted its subcommittee assignments as one slate.

why_it_matters: Lifting the freeze lets budgeted jobs be filled, but the business manager described the budget as very tight, so new positions and overlap hires for retirements face limits that bear on school spending and future tax requests.
The carried-over purchase orders and the no-increase salary schedule for unaffiliated staff show where FY21 school money is already committed, ahead of union negotiations.
watch_next: A special meeting on 48-hour notice once state transportation and sports guidance is released, plus a second August workshop date to be set by Doodle poll.
Union contract negotiations, which the committee took into executive session at the end of the meeting.
